# Compress Media

> Self-hosted compressor for video, images and audio (ffmpeg + sharp), with a drag-and-drop web UI, a CLI (`compress-media`) and a JSON HTTP API. Uploads are chunked and resumable, and can go straight to S3-compatible storage. Docker image: runsnip/compress-media (linux/amd64, linux/arm64). MIT licensed.

Which interface to use:

- **CLI:** local files, scripts and agents. No server needed; results are written next to the inputs as `<name>-compressed.<ext>`.
- **HTTP API:** a running server shared by several users or apps.
- **Web UI:** people.

## Using it

- [README](README.md): overview, quick start for every interface, platform support, recommended settings
- [CLI reference](docs/cli.md): commands (compress, probe, info, serve), every flag, JSON report, exit codes
- [HTTP API reference](docs/api.md): endpoints, chunked upload protocol (local vs direct-to-S3), job lifecycle, option objects, status codes
- [Example API clients](examples/): `compress.sh` (bash + curl + jq) and `compress.mjs` (Node.js 20+)

## Running it

- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): every environment variable (server, uploads, storage, binaries)
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): native, Docker, Compose, reverse proxy (Caddy/nginx), object storage per provider, CORS, lifecycle, IAM, scaling limits
- [Security](SECURITY.md): deployment model (no built-in auth), reporting vulnerabilities

## Agent skills

- [compress-media skill](skills/compress-media/SKILL.md): compress files for a user, choose settings from the goal, read the report, safety rules
- [compress-media reference](skills/compress-media/reference.md): full CLI flags, JSON fields, HTTP API with a CLI-flag → API-field table
- [compress-media-deploy skill](skills/compress-media-deploy/SKILL.md): install, configure, expose, upgrade and troubleshoot a server
